**GIUSEPPE FALCO IS NOT IN IT — AND GENERATION FOUR IS.**

**ACT 92, 20 NOVEMBER 1847 — VINCENZA FALCO**, born at twenty-one hours in her father's own house on **strada CAMELLARA**, to **RAFFAELE FALCO, thirty, contadino**, and **ANGELA ROSA MORGILLO, twenty-nine**. Baptised at Sant'Andrea the next day; witnesses **RAFFAELE CRISPI, forty, of strada Camellara**, and **ANGELO ZIMBARDO, forty-one**.

**THAT IS GENERATION FOUR, AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD NO HOUSEHOLD FOR IT.** Raffaele Falco was born 10 May 1818 and married Angela Rosa Morgillo in 1844; **their first documented child was generation five's CARMINE ANTONIO, born 10 July 1850.** **Vincenza is two years and eight months older** — and **the family tree names her, unsourced, as Raffaele's daughter.** *An assertion this archive carried as unverified is now a document.* **Both stated ages are exact**: thirty against a birth of 10 May 1818, twenty-nine against 24 February 1818.

**AND THE NEGATIVE THE ROW NEEDED.** «*Di anni UNO*» on 2 June 1848 puts **GIUSEPPE FALCO's** birth between **3 June 1846 and 2 June 1847**. **Both volumes are now read at the parents band and neither holds a MARIA MORGILLO.** Three things remain possible and this archive prefers none: **the stated age is wrong**, which these clerks do constantly; **the act was never drawn**; or **he was not born at Arienzo**.

**The 1847 tavola is under the archivist's card** — image 113, «*THIS INDEX HAS BEEN MICROFILMED ALREADY*», a sheet across the leaf with only a sliver of the act-number column showing. **That is the seventh volume with that card**: 1816, 1823, 1824, 1825, 1830, 1846, 1847.

*Noted in passing and not chased: **ANGELA MORGILLO, forty**, wife of the declarant of act 54 — the same forename as generation four's wife and a different woman; **MADDALENA DI GUIDA** at image 9; and an **ANGELA BIONDO** whose act carries her own 1883 marriage in its margin, «*sposò in ARIENZO DOMENICO DI LUCIA*», out of the lost years.*

**TWO FALCO CHILDREN BORN ON ONE DAY, TO TWO HOUSEHOLDS ON ONE STREET, AND THE ARCHIVE HAD NEITHER ACT.**

**ACT 42, 24 MARCH 1830 at six in the morning — PASQUALE FALCO**, in his father's own house on **strada CAMELLARA**, to **VINCENZO FALCO, thirty-eight, contadino**, and **ANDREANA CRISCI, thirty**. **This archive held him from a machine-read parish baptism and a death act; the civil act is new**, and it confirms the baptism's date of 24 March from an independent document. Witnesses **FRANCESCO CRISCI, forty, contadino of strada CRISCI** — the mother's surname, on the street that carries it, with no relationship word and none claimed — and **VINCENZO MORGILLO, thirty**.

**ACT 43, 24 MARCH 1830 at eleven — ANNA FALCO**, to **MICHELANGELO FALCO, twenty, contadino**, and **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA, twenty-five**, also of **strada CAMELLARA**, presented by the midwife **ROSA DELLA SELVA, seventy-nine**. **New.** Her death act, already held, says «*di mesi TREDICI*» on 4 May 1831 — **born 24 March 1830 she was thirteen months and ten days.** This household's whole documented life is now three acts: a wedding in December 1828, this birth, and this death.

**AND THE TWO BANDS EACH FOUND ONE.** Act 42 says «*e da lui dichiarante*» — **the left page names ANDREANA CRISCI and no Falco**, so only the declarant band could see it. Act 43 was presented by a midwife — **so only the parents band names its father.** **Neither band alone would have found both children**, in a year whose *tavola* cannot be read at all.

## THE TAVOLA IS BLOCKED — THE FOURTH VOLUME WITH THE SAME CARD

Image **148** carries the closing certificate on the left, signed **VITO MARIA ROMANO** on 31 December 1830 for «*fogli scritti num. CENTOQUARANTATRE, contenente atti num. CENTOQUARANTATRE*» — and on the right the index leaf with **«THIS INDEX HAS BEEN MICROFILMED ALREADY»** across its foot. **1823, 1824, 1825, 1830 and 1846 now carry that card.** See work-list row 10.

**Michelangelo Falco is TWENTY here**, against twenty-six in July 1832 and thirty-four in September 1838 — **fourteen years of ageing in eight**, which is why his identity across those acts cannot be settled by age. **Vincenzo Falco is thirty-eight, exact against his baptism of 1 February 1792.**

**Images 1–146 read; the year is declared overwhelmingly by ROSA DELLA SELVA, seventy-nine, and CATERINA RUGGIERO, seventy-two**, with **GELSOMINA RUGGIERO, sixty**, and, at the very end of the year, **FELICIELLA MARTONE, forty**, who will carry 1837 on her own.

**FIVE FALCO IN THE YEAR, AND TWO OF THEM ARE NEW — both through FALCO MOTHERS.**

**ACT 52, 27 APRIL — ALESSANDRA DIGLIO**, to **ALFONSO DIGLIO, twenty-seven, contadino of strada CAMELLARA**, and **MARIA FALCO, twenty-seven**. **New**, and it pushes that household back three years from 1822. **Her father signed his own name** — «*firmato da noi, **e dal dichiarante**, avendo i testimonj asserito di non sapere scrivere*», and at the foot, in block capitals, **«A ALFONSO DIGLIO»**. *Both witnesses could not write and he could.*

**ACT 68, 7 JUNE — GIUSEPPE CIOFFI**, to **FRANCESCO CIOFFI, twenty-four**, and **MARIA FALCO, twenty-three**, of strada Camellara. **New — and this archive held him only as a death**: 25 March 1824, aged five. **Born 7 June 1819 he was five years and nine months.** It is also the earliest sighting of that household by three years.

**Already held, and all three confirmed from the image**: **act 33, 18 March — DOMENICO CLEMENTE FALCO**, to Giuseppe Falco, thirty-eight, *massaro di campagna*, and Gelsomina Vigliotta; **act 99, 11 October — CRESCENZO FALCO**, to Giuseppe Falco, forty, *contadino*, and Antonia di Guida; **act 134, 21 December — LUIGI FALCO**, to **VINCENZO FALCO, twenty-six**, and Andreana Crisci.

**TWO GIUSEPPE FALCO ON STRADA CAMELLARA IN ONE YEAR, SEVEN MONTHS APART** — thirty-eight and a *massaro di campagna* in March, forty and a *contadino* in October, one married to a Vigliotta and one to a di Guida. **The street has never told them apart**, and this archive had published that it stopped doing so in 1823. On /corrections.

## AND THE REGISTER RECORDS ONE OF ITS OWN ERRORS, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN A FIND

Image **59** carries a *notamento* of **4 January 1839**: «*con deliberazione del Tribunale … del dì ventiuno … Dicembre … mille ottocento **trentotto**, essendosi ordinata la **rettifica dell'errore** d'incorso nell'atto di nascita di **ANGELA ROSA COSSI** … descritto sotto il numero d'ordine **CENTOQUATTORDICI** del presente registro, spiegandosi di esser costei **nata da ANGELO COSSI, e da PAOLA BELELLA, e non già da PAOLA VERDICCHIO come sta scritto in esso***».

**A clerk wrote the wrong maternal surname into a birth act, and it took a court order nineteen years later to correct it.** This archive reads Falco women out of that same line — «*e da MARIA FALCO sua moglie legittima*» — in act after act. **The register itself is the authority for saying that line can simply be wrong**, and this is the first time it has said so in a volume read here. *No Falco act is under suspicion on this account; it is recorded because the possibility is now documented rather than theoretical.*

**The 1819 tavola is incomplete in the film.** Only its **last page, numbered XI**, is photographed, on image **74**, and the child's-name column is lost in the gutter; the parents' column and the dates survive. Pages I–X are not in this filming. **Images 1–72 hold the acts; 73 is blank.**

**ACT 28, 8 MARCH 1828 — MARIANTONIA CIOFFI**, born at fifteen hours in her father's own house on **strada CAMELLARA**, to **FRANCESCO CIOFFI, thirty, contadino**, and **MARIA FALCO, thirty**. **Her death act, already held, says «*di mesi SETTE*» on 23 October 1828** — born 8 March, she was seven months and fifteen days. **The arithmetic is exact.** Witnesses **NICOLA CIOFFI, twenty-six, *sartore*, of strada Camellara**, and **ANDREA DIGLIO, twenty-one, of strada Saponari**; the *sindaco* who signs is **SAVERIO CIOFFI**.

**ACT 118, 19 DECEMBER 1828 — SARA FALCO**, to **VINCENZO FALCO** and **ANDREANA CRISCI, twenty-seven**, of strada Camellara. **Already held**, and the citation is confirmed from both the act and the index.

## THE TAVOLA IS COMPLETE, AND IT CLOSES THE OTHER HALF OF THE QUESTION

The 1828 *tavola alfabetica annuale* runs from image 126 and is filled, with **both parents named on every line**. Its F group, page **XVI**, holds **one entry**: «*118. **Falco Sara** | **Falco Vincenzo, e Crisci Andreana** | A 19 Xbre 1828*», followed immediately by *Giglio*, *Guida*, *Gagliardo*, *Gesuè* and *Lettieri* — so the page-break rule is satisfied.

**A COMPLETE TAVOLA MAKES THE DECLARANT BAND REDUNDANT, AND THIS ROW SAYS SO RATHER THAN RUNNING IT.** A Falco **father**'s child is surnamed Falco and is filed under F; **the index answers that question outright**. What an index cannot answer is a Falco **mother**, whose child is filed under her husband's surname — which is why act 28 needed the parents band and why it had never been found. *The declarant band was swept and not read, on that reasoning, and the sheets are kept.*

## FOUR DI GUIDA, AND NONE OF THEM CLAIMED

The di Guida of Arienzo are an open line here — **Antonia di Guida** married the founder's son — and this volume shows four of the name without joining any of them: **LUIGI DI GUIDA and CHIARA RIVETTI**, of strada Monticello de' Cappuccini, whose son **MARCELLO** is act 44; **FAUSTINA DI GUIDA, twenty-seven, of strada CAMELLARA**, wife of Angelo Zimbardo; and **ROSA DI GUIDA, twenty-four**. With **VITTORIA DI GUIDA, forty, of strada Camellara** from the 1827 register, that is four women and one man of the name on or beside the Falco's own street in two years. **Nothing is claimed.**

**Images 1–123 read; 124 blank; the closing certificate is 125 and the tavola runs 126–133.**

*A birth at **SAN FELICE A CANCELLO** is registered here at image 112 — **FELICIELLA ATTARELLI, twenty-five, of strada Carnola**, wife of a Nicola Morgillo. Noted because generation four's wife was born at San Felice; **nothing is claimed**.*

src: Arienzo BIRTH registers — the annual tavole. ANTENATI an_ua14428 (1831), an_ua14429 (1832), an_ua14433 (1836) and an_ua14434 (1837).
what: Whether the Arienzo birth volumes of the 1830s carry a usable alphabetical tavola, which is the cheap way to find one child in a year of 130 births
got:
**THEY ARE SPORADIC, AND THEY FAIL IN THREE DIFFERENT WAYS.**

**1831 has no tavola at all.** `an_ua14428` ends with its last acts — 244, 245, 246, all late December — then two blank leaves and the Procuratore del Re's certificate.

**1836 has one and it was never filled in.** `an_ua14433` image 127 right carries the printed heading «*Tavola alfabetica annuale de' Nati per l'anno milleottocento*» over its ruled columns, and every cell is empty.

**1832 has one, filled, and it stops at C.** `an_ua14429` image 116 gives «*Circondario di Arienzo — Tavola alfabetica annuale de' Nati per l'anno milleottocento trentadue 1832*», with **Numero d'ordine · Cognomi e Nomi degli Nati · Cognomi e Nomi de' genitori · Giorno della Nascita · Osservazioni**, and it runs Anzivino, Andrea, Arrigale, Ambrosio, Bernardo, Balletta, Crisci, Cimmino — and the volume ends. **F is not in it.**

**That last shape is one this archive has met before**: the 1834 death index is «a single leaf covering A to C and marked END». **An Arienzo index that stops at C is a pattern, not an accident**, and a search that reaches the C page and finds nothing has not reached F at all.

**So the tavola cannot be trusted as the cheap route in this decade**, and a year must be read at the parents band — about seven contact sheets for 120 images.

**AND 1837 MAKES IT A PATTERN RATHER THAN A RUN OF BAD LUCK.** Its tavola is at image 144, headed and filled — Arrigale, Affinito, Ambrosio, Amone, Andreana, Altarelli, Anzivino, Bernardo, Cospi, Carfora, Cimmino — and **ends at C**. Image 145 is a **duplicate photograph of 144 with the Archivio's own conservation slip lying across the page**, and 146 closes the volume. **The rest of the alphabet was never filmed.**

**So: 1831 none, 1836 blank, 1832 and 1837 filled and stopping at C** — and the 1834 death index is «a single leaf covering A to C and marked END». **An Arienzo index of this period that reaches C has not reached F**, and for a family called FALCO that is the whole of the difference.

## SARA RUGGIERO WAS A MIDWIFE

**Act 29, 27 February 1816**: «*è comparsa **SARA RUGGIERO, di anni QUARANTACINQUE, di professione LEVATRICE, domiciliata in detto Comune, strada CAMELLARA***». She appears again in the same volume, presenting a child for a *possidente*'s household on strada dell'Annunziata.

**This archive holds a SARA RUGGIERO, forty-five, of strada CAMELLARA, in the 1817 register** — there she is the wife of **ARCANGELO CRISCI** and the mother of **ANDREANA CRISCI**, generation three's wife. **Forty-five in February 1816 and forty-five in 1817, one street, one name.** *The identification is set down as an identification, not as a quotation; no act says both things in one sentence.*

**AND IT EXPLAINS THE TEN PAGES.** «*Matrina fuit SARA RUGGIERO*» stands on **ten pages** of the Arienzo parish baptism harvest, godmother to children of **at least six Falco households**, and this archive had no account of that reach. **A levatrice stands godmother to the children she delivers.** Her presence across six unrelated Falco houses is her trade, not a kinship — an inference this archive was careful never to draw and now need not.

**THREE RUGGIERO WOMEN DELIVERED THIS TOWN.** **SARA RUGGIERO**, forty-five here; **CATERINA RUGGIERO**, **sixty in this same volume** and seventy-five by 1833; and **GELSOMINA RUGGIERO**, who appears from 1826. *Three midwives of one surname across twenty years. Nothing is claimed about how they were related, and the name is common at Arienzo — but generation three's mother-in-law is one of them.*

## AND A CORROBORATION FOR THE 1839 RECTIFICATION

The 1819 register carries a court-ordered *rettifica* of 1838 stating that a child was born «*da **ANGELO COSSI**, e da **PAOLA BELELLA**, e non già da PAOLA VERDICCHIO*». **This volume has the couple**: image 38 right, **ANGELO COSSI, thirty-seven, bracciale of strada CAMELLARA**, and **PAOLA BELELLA, twenty-seven**. **The correction was right and the original act was wrong**, and an independent document three years earlier says so.

The closing certificate gives the year at **123 acts**.

src: The National Archives (UK), Discovery — discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk, 17 September 2026. The catalogue over TNA's own holdings at Kew plus some 2,500 other British archives. Every surname in this archive searched.
what: Falco, Zampiello, Annecchino, Arricale, Carfora, Crisci, Morgillo, Rivetti — and the three towns, Arienzo, Forchia, Arpaia
got:
**A CLEAN NIL FOR THE FAMILY, AND ONE RECORD ABOUT THE TOWN.**

**ZAMPIELLO 0 · ANNECCHINO 0 · ARRICALE 0 · CARFORA 0 · MORGILLO 0 · RIVETTI 0 · CRISCI 1 · FORCHIA 0 · ARPAIA 0.**

**FALCO returns 86, and not one of them can be this family.** They are British records of people who happened to bear the name: **eighteen WO service records** of British soldiers (service numbers, dates of birth 1903–1925); **twenty-one BT records** of merchant seamen registered at UK ports — «*R360597 FALCO J 11/10/1926 LONDON*», «*R542406 FALCO A 16/08/1917 SANTIAGO, CHILE*»; **twelve HO files**, mostly naturalisation certificates of Italians resident in Britain, the nearest being **Luigi Falco, born 17 July 1894 at SAVIANO**; a company dissolved in 1995; a lawsuit of 1515; and a Lake Como steamer. **«Falco Arienzo» returns 0. «Falco Caserta» returns 0.**

**This family has no British generation, and the catalogue confirms it rather than merely failing to contradict it.** The path is Arienzo → Forchia → Arpaia → Naples → Brisbane, and nobody on it registered as an alien, served the Crown, or signed on at a British port.

**BUT ONE FILE NAMES THE TOWN, AND IT IS WORTH ORDERING.** **WO 32/22147**, 1–31 March 1945: «*Special Investigation Branch investigation: alleged murder of Herron FG, Private, 1583838, Argyle and Sutherland Highlanders **by two Italian civilians at ARIENZO, Italy, 11 March 1945***». Open since 25 August 2017, held at Kew, **not digitised**. A British military police file about a killing in this family's town, five months before the war ended, which would name the accused and its witnesses. **It is a lead about Arienzo, not about the Falco, and it is recorded as that.**

src: Arienzo, «Registro degli atti diversi» — ANTENATI, 45 volumes, `an_ua14064`–`an_ua14106` plus `an_ua57637`–`57638`. The register of births at sea, recognitions, adoptions, PEOPLE WHO DIED AWAY FROM THEIR OWN HOME, and stillbirths. Read end to end, 17–20 September 2026.
what: FALCO and DI GUIDA — and in particular the deaths of ANTONIA DI GUIDA, alive 2 February 1845, and GIUSEPPE FALCO of Antonia di Guida, alive 26 November 1849
got:
**NO FALCO IN ANY OF THE FORTY-FIVE VOLUMES, AND NO DI GUIDA.** Every act from **1845 to 1865** is read and its dead are named — the whole window either person could fall in. Four acts in the series remain unnamed, all **before 1845**, so neither can be among them.

**When an Arienzo person died elsewhere, the comune where they died drew the act and sent a certified copy home, and Arienzo copied it in whole** — age, trade, street, both parents, whether they were dead, surviving children with their ages. So this was the one instrument that could hold a death the town never recorded. **It does not hold theirs.**

**What it does hold is about thirty-five deaths away from home, and they map where an Arienzo labourer went and did not come back from**: the **Ospedale degli Incurabili** at Naples (5), **Sant'Agostino degli Scalzi** at Aversa (3), the **Real Stabilimento de' Matti** and its women's side at Aversa (6), **Acerra** (3), **Caserta** (2), **Airola** (2), a masseria in the **Nola** district, **Montesarchio**, **Santa Maria Maggiore**, the **Ospedale della Trinità** — and once, **LIPARI**.

**PASQUALE PORRINO**, 52, a labourer born at Arienzo, died **31 October 1864 in the hospital of the DOMICILIATI COATTI on Lipari** — internal exile. **CARLO BALLETTA**, soldier of the **1st Dragoons**, died in the Ospedale della Trinità on 3 March 1855, his colonel writing to ask the sindaco to tell his family to collect **one ducat and thirty-five grana**, the price of his kit. **ANGELO IMBIMBO**, 60, died in the Aversa madhouse on 30 November 1855 — and **FRANCESCO IMBIMBO, «figlio d'Angelo»**, died in the **same asylum** on 4 November 1844. **Father and son, eleven years apart.**

**TWO CAUTIONS FOR ANYONE FOLLOWING.** The holdings query `localita=Arienzo` matches **several comuni** — Corpo d'Arienzo, **San Felice d'Arienzo**, **San Casale di Arienzo** — and the printed title page gives the CIRCONDARIO at the top, which is the district, not the town. **Read the comune from each volume's own title page.** And **from 1856 the clerk leaves the printed act heading blank and writes only the body**, so a sweep of the heading band reports «no acts» for a volume holding five.

src: Arienzo PROCESSETTI (marriage supplements), 1860 — ANTENATI `an_ua14207`, 479 images. **Bundle 3 read out, images 25–42.** The first Arienzo processetti bundle this archive has opened since the 1814 and 1815 volumes.
what: The eight documents behind the marriage of **SABBATINO ANNECCHINO of Forchia** and **MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA of Arienzo**, 21 January 1860 — and in particular item 4, «*l'atto di morte dell'AVO PATERNO*», a generation the marriage act never names
got:
**SEVEN OF THE EIGHT DOCUMENTS ARE THERE, AND THEY CARRY FOUR GENERATIONS.**

**Item 1** — the groom's birth: **Forchia, Nati 1825, act 5, 20 February 1825**, presented by **Carmine Annecchino, forty, bracciale, contrada detta li Preti**, mother **Rosa Ceglia**, thirty; baptised at **San Nicola** the same day.

**Item 2** — **Forchia, Morti 1838, act 20, 8 August 1838**: **CARMINE ANNECCHINO**, fifty-two, colono of the **Masseria de' Preti**, «*figlio di **ANTONIO ANNECCHINO defunto** … e di **MARIA GUIDA defunta***».

**Item 3** — **Forchia, Morti 1852, act 4, 4 April 1852**: **ROSA CEGLIA, vedova di Carmine Annecchino**, sixty-two, ***filatrice***, **born at ARPAIA**, «*figlia di **ANTONIO CEGLIA defunto** … e di **GRAZIA VITAGLIANO defunta***». Declared in part by **NICOLA ANNECCHINO**, forty-four, of the same masseria.

**Item 4 — the generation this bundle was opened for.** **Forchia, Morti 1826, act 8, 14 June 1826**: **ANTONIO ANNECCHINO**, born Forchia, **seventy-three**, bracciale, «*figlio di **DOMENICO ANNECCHINO defunto** … e di **ELISABETTA D'ONOFRIO defunta***». **Filed twice, images 30 and 31, identical.**

**Item 5** — the bride's birth extract, **Arienzo act 142 of 1830**. *Used to locate the act and then set aside: the register itself was read.*

**Item 6** — the father's consent, Arienzo, **1 January 1860**, naming **FRANCESCO CARFORA** in full and **overturning this archive's «VALERIO»**.

**Item 8** — the notifications posted at Arienzo on **Sunday 1 January 1860**.

**ITEM 7 IS NOT IN THE BUNDLE.** «*Nell'atto di morte della madre della stessa*» — **PASQUA MORGILLO's death act** — should be an **Arienzo** paper. Images 25 to 42 hold **four death extracts and all four are from Forchia**. It is not misfiled in the bundle's tail, which is notifications and prose. **Recorded as a nil so the bundle is not re-read for it.**

what: **ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO's birth act**, act 66, named by the certified copy in her 1845 marriage dossier

**1865, act 3, 23 January — ANGELA FALCO**, twenty-eight, born Arienzo, marrying **VINCENZO ABATIELLO**, forty, *contadino* of **LIVERI**. «*figlia di **MATTEO FALCO**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi**, e di **ALESSANDRA CRISCI**, domiciliata **ivi***». **A child of Matteo Falco and Alessandra Crisci this archive did not have**, born about **1837**; **both her parents alive**; and **her mother's surname spelled out**, which the 1846 birth act of her sister Domenica left deliberately unread.

**1861, act of 19 September — STANISLAO FALCO** × **FILOMENA DI LUCIA**, which this archive already holds. *The name band read it as «Francesco Falco»; the **notification register bound into the same volume** settles it — «*matrimonio tra **STANISLAO FALCO** figlio di **VINCENZO** e di **ANDREANA CRISCI** e **FILOMENA DI LUCIA**… figlia di **LUIGI** e di **MARIA DI NUZZO***» — and it is one more strip reading overturned by a second document in the same hour.*

**1862, 1863 and 1864 hold no Falco at all** — twenty-seven, twenty-two and twenty-six acts, every one read.

**NEITHER GIUSEPPE FALCO NOR ANTONIA DI GUIDA IS NAMED IN ANY OF THE FIVE YEARS**, alive or dead. Rows 39 and 40 are not answered here.

**THE INSTRUMENT, FOR WHOEVER TAKES 1850–1860.** Band `--band 0.26 0.26 --half R --cols 2 --width 2600`: it carries the groom, **both his parents**, the bride, **both her parents**, and which of the four the act marks dead — twelve or fourteen acts to a sheet. **And where a volume carries its notification register too** (1861 does, images 31–76), the notifications list each couple and all four parents in three lines, which is cheaper still and is the control on a doubtful reading.

*The sweep also turned up **ANTONIO CARFORA, thirty-three, contadino of **strada SIGNORINDICO**, son of **GIOVANNI CARFORA defunto** and **CATERINA BIONDILLO defunta**, marrying **GIUSTINA CARFORA**, twenty-six, in December 1850 — a fifth Carfora household head for that street, recorded and not joined to any other.*

**TWO SISTERS, TWENTY-SEVEN MONTHS APART, AND BETWEEN THEM THEIR MOTHER DIED.** Antonia di Guida's window was **2 February 1845 to 1865, twenty years wide**. **1857, act 28, 26 November — MARIA CARMELA FALCO**, twenty-five, of Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci, marrying **NICOLA DI LUCIA of San Felice**. *Her brother Stanislao married a Filomena di Lucia four years later.*

**SO ANTONIA DI GUIDA DID NOT DIE AT ARIENZO** — or her death was never entered in its civil register. *This archive's fifteen-year read of the Arienzo deaths, 1844 to 1858, was made hunting FALCO; it was never run for GUIDA. **AND THE F SECTIONS WERE RE-DERIVED, NOT DISCOVERED.** 1859's three Falco — **MARIA** (act 19, 4 March), **CARMELA** (act 55, 4 August) and **RAFFAELE** (act 60, 17 August), all children of a **MICHELE FALCO** — were published here on **14 September 2026** from this same tavola, and re-announcing them was withdrawn as a discovery on the 15th. **`tools/isitnew.py` caught it a third time today before a word was written.**

what: **RAFFAELA FALCO**, born about 1813 to **GIUSEPPE FALCO** and **ANTONIA DI GUIDA** — the test work-list row 87 named as cheaper than the three it had first listed

**SHE IS NOT IN IT. FIFTY-THREE ACTS, ONE FALCO, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT HOUSE.**

**Act 2, 5 January 1813** — «*è comparso **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di anni **trentatré**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato in detto Comune, **strada COSTA** … da **GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA** sua moglie legittima, di anni **ventotto**, un **maschio** … a cui si è dato il nome di **ANTONIO***». **The OTHER Giuseppe Falco** — of strada Costa, not of Antonia di Guida — and **ANTONIO FALCO is a child that household did not have**, four years earlier than anything else it holds.

**No Raffaela Falco. No Antonia di Guida. No second Falco of any kind.** The year is otherwise Cioffi, Figlio, Morgillo, Verrecchia, Rivetti, Saccone and Arricale, with four acts presented by the *levatrici* **Rosa della Selva** and **Caterina Ruggiero**.

**So the 1812–1814 window for Raffaela Falco is down to 1812 and 1814** — `an_ua14409` (93 images) and `an_ua14411` (66). *Nineteen in July 1832 means born between July 1812 and July 1813, so **1812** is the one to read next, and its second half first.*

**A PRACTICAL NOTE FOR THE OTHER SIX VOLUMES OF THIS DECADE.** The band is `--band 0.13 0.25 --half LR --cols 3 --width 2600`, nine images to a sheet. **At four columns the names are gone** — and a negative off an illegible sheet is worth nothing, which is the whole reason this row exists.
